# ModularPipelines 4.0

ModularPipelines 4.0 consolidates module configuration, makes pipeline options immutable, and
standardizes the public API. It is a breaking release: follow the
[v3 to v4 migration guide](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/migrating-to-v4)
before upgrading from 3.2.8.

## Upgrading

- Upgrade every ModularPipelines package your pipeline uses to 4.0.0 together, including custom
  integration projects and test helpers.
- Pipeline projects now target .NET 11, with C# 14 or later for the generated
  `context.Tools.<Tool>` properties. The applications your pipeline builds can keep their own
  target frameworks.
- Add `.modularpipelines/run-history/` to `.gitignore`, or disable history with
  `RunReport.HistoryRetention = 0`. Run reports are now saved by default.

## Breaking changes

The six biggest changes:

1. Register modules on `builder`, then use `await builder.RunAsync()` or
   `await builder.BuildAsync()`. `Build()` and `ExecutePipelineAsync()` are gone, and building
   now validates the pipeline.
2. Replace mutable `builder.Options` assignments with
   `builder.ConfigureOptions(options => options with { ... })`.
3. Override `void Configure(ModuleConfigurationBuilder module)` and move dependencies, retries,
   and metadata into it.
4. Import `ModularPipelines` for core authoring types and use `context.Tools.<Tool>` for
   integrations.
5. Use `Task<T>` for `Module<T>`, typed result variants, and `summary.Results`.
6. Use `Async` command methods, `cancellationToken:`, and the regenerated CLI option contracts.

```csharp
var builder = Pipeline.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.AddModule<BuildModule>().AddModule<TestModule>();
await builder.RunAsync();
```

Some changes need checking even after the code compiles:

- A required dependency that is skipped now skips its consumers too.
- HTTP retries default to idempotent methods only; 3.x retried every method.
- Commands now time out after 30 minutes by default; 3.x tool commands had no command-level limit
  unless `ExecutionTimeout` was set. Set a longer `ExecutionTimeout`, or `null` for no limit.
  Module timeouts apply to each retry attempt rather than the whole sequence.
- Command results capture at most 1,048,576 characters per output stream by default.
- Canceled commands terminate their descendant processes.
- OpenTelemetry module status values are lowercase snake_case, such as `succeeded` and
  `timed_out`.
- `IsBuildServer` is now `IsCI`, and it also honors a truthy `CI` environment variable.

The migration guide covers the
[full list of runtime behavior changes](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/migrating-to-v4#runtime-behavior-changes),
a [breaking API reference](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/migrating-to-v4#breaking-api-reference),
and a [reference for automated migrations](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/migrating-to-v4#agents--llm-migration-reference).

## New in 4.0

- [Pipeline CLI](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/how-to/command-line): module
  selection, validation, and dry-run planning.
- [Fingerprint-based caching](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/how-to/module-caching),
  with a pipeline-wide switch to disable it.
- [Run reports and local history](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/how-to/run-reports),
  including duration comparisons against earlier runs.
- [OpenTelemetry](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/how-to/opentelemetry),
  dependency graph export, and richer CI output.
- [Distributed execution](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/distributed/architecture)
  across workers, with artifact contracts and worker capabilities.
- [Trimming and Native AOT support](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/how-to/native-aot)
  for supported, statically described C# pipelines.
- [Testing helpers](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/how-to/testing), including
  command interceptors, and [F# module support](https://modularpipelines.tomlonghurst.dev/docs/how-to/fsharp).
- Additional CLI integrations and much wider command coverage in the existing ones.

## Feedback

Search or open a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/thomhurst/ModularPipelines/issues) with the old
and new package versions, a minimal module or command example, and the compiler or runtime error.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/thomhurst/ModularPipelines/compare/v3.2.8...v4.0.0
